_contract: Every value under `probes` MUST be a single literal SELECT/WITH that returns one row carrying an `expected` and an `observed` column. The bridge (scripts/remediation_contract_bridge.py) rejects anything else to the `needs-machine-probe` sentinel, so a malformed entry degrades to 'inactive', never to a false pass. Do NOT add a probe whose observed value is derived from its expected value, and do NOT add a probe that returns a constant.
_provenance: Every probe in this map was executed against qnfo-audit before commit. Entries were kept only when observed != expected at authoring time, so each one reports its defect as STILL PRESENT. A probe that passed on first execution was deliberately omitted: a passing probe auto-closes the issue via the armed triggers, so a probe that passes without the defect being fixed would falsify the record. See the commit message for the exclusion list and the reason for each exclusion.
_timestamp_formats: Audit timestamps are NOT uniform. Most are ISO-8601 with a literal 'T' (device_tasks, fleet_agents, report_card_inputs, venue_radar_runs, events_radar, conference_radar, social_engagements) and are normalised with replace(substr(col,1,19),'T',' '). paper_explain_log and publications use a space separator, for which the same expression is a harmless no-op. proof_events.ts is epoch-MILLISECONDS and must be divided by 1000 and read as 'unixepoch'. Getting this wrong yields a 1970 comparison that silently mis-grades the probe.
_transport_limit: The consumer's d1() resolves a single database (REMEDIATION_DB, default qnfo-audit). A probe therefore CANNOT reference another bound database. Issues whose only evidence lives in personal / outreach / living / graph / portfolio / cms / ipatent are unmappable here and stay 'needs-machine-probe' until a cross-database transport exists.
